_note: MCP server template. Copy to data/mcp_servers.json (the app reads that path on startup); data/ is gitignored, so your keys stay local. Each entry is its own subprocess, and `command` is resolved against the app's PATH — a bare "python" means THE APP'S interpreter.
_note_venv: A server that needs a different mcp SDK version runs in its own venv and points `command` at that venv's python.exe by absolute path (see vision). Do not upgrade the app's mcp instead: amap-mcp-server pins mcp==1.8.1, and mcp>=1.30 on Python 3.14 needs starlette>=0.48 while fastapi needs <0.47 — the conflict is structural (ADR-0010).
_note_vision: The vision server must be named `vision` unless you set VISION_MCP_TOOL in .env to its actual tool name (e.g. mcp__my-server__analyze_image); otherwise see_screen silently falls back to the legacy vision model.
_note_vision_env: deepseek_vision_mcp reads VISION_* (not ZHIPU_API_KEY) and also loads a .env of its own, so pin base_url/model here: the app's .env holds the legacy qwen vision settings and would otherwise win. glm-4.6v-flash is the free Zhipu vision model — it can answer 429/1305 (free-tier congestion) transiently, which is a provider condition, not a wiring problem. PYTHONIOENCODING keeps its Chinese log lines readable on Windows.
